findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy for the facility. Provided copy of policy. PIC indicated he would laminate the policy for the back kitchen area near the mop sink. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed the bar hand sink to have many mixed drinks dumped into the sink (ice, sliced fruit, straws). Discussed with multiple employees that the hand sink is for hand washing ONLY and must not be used as a dump sink. Employee cleaned the hand sink (wash, rinse, sanitize) - COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure. 

(REPEAT) Observed the microwave to be soiled. Microwave had burnt food on the rotating plate and food splash within the interior walls. Discussed with employees that microwaves should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 24 hours or more as needed. Employee cleaned during the inspection. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 2/13/20 and 12/17/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Underneath of the 3 compartment sink and hand sink a the bar has piles of straws, old cans, and debris. Ensure staff is cleaning under the bar to inhibit pests.
2. Kitchen should have equipment pulled from walls on a routine schedule to clean food debris (food splash, burnt pizza debris, etc). Area behind the fryers had food debris and grease. Pizza ovens had burnt pizza crumbs behind. 

Discussed routine cleaning schedule with PIC. Ensure staff abides and cleans areas mentioned as needed to prevent debris build-up.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses for the facility. Ensure all new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Discussed with PIC. Ensure copies are left at the facility in the public health folder or binder. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/17/21.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Inspector will follow-up on 1/10/22.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager for the facility. Facility is using regional manager’s because there is no permanent local manager. Ensure a manager has a valid CFPM license. Keep copy at the facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at three compartment sink. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed 3 compartment sink to measure at 100 ppm of quat sanitizer after multiple attempts of testing with test strips. Inspector advised PIC to call EcoLab in order to service the dispenser of the 3 compartment sink. PIC called during inspection. EcoLab will perform service tomorrow, 2/14/20. Inspector instructed facility to manually pour sanitizer out of bags into the 3 compartment sink and sani buckets until the dispenser is serviced. Inspector will follow-up on 2/17/20.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12  (C) Interior of microwave is heavily soiled. Interior cavity and door seals of microwaves must be cleaned and sanitized at least once every 24 hours. Reference 4-602.12.

Observed interior of microwave to be soiled. PIC indicated staff should be cleaning the microwave as part of nightly procedures. Discussed cleaning and sanitizing interior of microwave at least every 24 hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items throughout facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple items throughout facility to lack date marking. Multiple boxes of shred cheese for pizza's were portioned into smaller bags, but lacked date marking. PIC knew when portioning took place and appropriately date marked items. Bacon was observed to be lacking date marking, as well as hot dogs. PIC dated marked hot dogs; however, the bacon was voluntarily discarded as PIC was unaware when it was pulled for the prep cooler. Discussed routine date marking with PIC and stressed the importance of discarding food within 7 days. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112  (C) Flies observed, dead, in the lighting of the clean dish storage area. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate flies, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.112.

Observed multiple dead flies in the lighting shield of the clean dish storage area. Discussed routine cleaning of pests within lighting shields. Advised facility to utilize pest control, as needed. Discussed routine pest control with PIC. Facility utilizes Terminex once a month.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.

Observed back exterior door near the ice machine to have a seal which is not solid and tight fitting; therefore, allows access to pests. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

Observed single-use articles to be stored in a manner that is not covered or inverted. PIC was educated on the importance of covering single-use items throughout facility. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on bottome cold holding units. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used

Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.
